tagline: From the desert floor to mile-high pines and down again.
intro: Out of Palm Desert, Highway 74 follows Carrizo Creek and climbs Deep Canyon, leaving the desert palms below for conifer country. It crosses the Santa Rosa Indian Reservation and runs through Garner Valley to Mountain Center. There Highway 243 turns north through Idyllwild and the forest, then makes a few switchbacks down toward Banning, with the San Gorgonio Wilderness off to the north.
Riverside County named it the Palms to Pines Highway in 1930. The road down to Banning is older. It was oiled and open by 1910, partly to haul lumber and to fight fires.

moments.title: Seven Level Hill
moments.text: The grade just south of Palm Desert where the cast of It's a Mad, Mad, Mad, Mad World first meet, over a car wreck, in the film's opening minutes.

moments.title: Pinyon Pines
moments.text: A small valley at about 4,000 feet, named for its trees. In the 1930s a mechanic, Art Nightingale, put up lodging here for the men building the highway, and a cafe, since closed.

moments.title: Idyllwild
moments.text: Mile-high Idyllwild, once Strawberry Valley, sits between Tahquitz Peak and Suicide Rock. For years it dressed as an alpine village with German-sounding names, a habit dropped during World War II.
